channel.title: GPT3 Marketing
channel.description: GPT3 Marketing is a generative-AI content consultancy est. 2020: brand voice systems, prompt libraries and human-edited content, grounded by SOMIN.

item.title: What few-shot prompting in 2020 still teaches content teams
item.description: GPT-3 forced writers to teach by example. Those few-shot habits remain the best defence against generic AI content in 2026.

item.title: Why AI content all sounds the same, and how to escape it
item.description: Generic AI copy comes from averaged inputs, not bad models. How to diagnose sameness and rebuild a voice your audience recognises.

item.title: How to build a brand voice system that AI can follow
item.description: A brand voice system for the AI era: principles, vocabulary, examples and model-ready instructions your writers and models both use.

item.title: Why AI drafts still need heavy editing, and how to need less
item.description: Heavy revision of AI drafts is usually an input problem. Where the editing time goes and how to move effort upstream.

item.title: From GPT-3 to ChatGPT: what really changed for marketers
item.description: Six years from the GPT-3 API beta to today: what changed for content teams, what did not, and why craft matters more now.

item.title: Prompt libraries: how to build, version and govern them
item.description: A practical guide to building a team prompt library: structure, versioning, testing, ownership and keeping it grounded in audience evidence.

item.title: Authenticity outlasts trends: narrative over FOMO in AI content
item.description: Trend-chasing with AI makes brands faster and blurrier. Why a consistent narrative compounds, and how to test trends against it.

item.title: Human-edited content at scale: roles, loops and limits
item.description: How to scale AI-assisted content without losing quality: editorial roles, review tiers, feedback loops and where humans add most value.

item.title: How to run a brand voice audit in the age of AI content
item.description: A step-by-step brand voice audit: gather samples, test distinctiveness, compare with audience language and prioritise fixes.

item.title: Audience-grounded AI content: feeding models what people say
item.description: Why AI content improves when briefs carry real audience language and tensions, and a practical workflow for grounding prompts in evidence.
